title: BiGym 2.0
subtitle: Benchmarking Learned and Agent-Developed Policies for Humanoid Household Manipulation
description: A Unitree G1 benchmark of 20 household tasks with a frozen whole-body controller in the loop, 60 human VR demonstrations per task, and a coding-agent track scored on the same hidden seeds as learned policies.
lede: BiGym 2.0 is a household loco-manipulation benchmark: 20 tasks on the Unitree G1, with 60 human VR demonstrations each.
From one demonstration, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 write controllers that beat every demo-driven RL baseline on the nine-task mean and rival imitation learning,
learned policies still lead on precise object rearrangement.

hero.alt: Twenty BiGym 2.0 tasks running side by side; the camera flies through the scenes and rises to an overview.

summary: BiGym 2.0: 20 household tasks on the Unitree G1 under whole-body control, with 60 human VR demonstrations per task.

Four kinds of policy on the same inputs and hidden seeds: vision-language-action fine-tuning, imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning, and coding agents that write a program from one demonstration.
Coding agents handle spatial variation well but struggle to keep physical contact; learned policies show the reverse, and multi-object transport stays hard for all of them.
